final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a more accurate, caveated interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is useful but not sufficient for compliant_with_caveats here, because the caveat is not a peripheral uncertainty; it is the unresolved policy predicate itself. The admissible evidence still shows a material issue affecting a named launch use case, an open legal review, and no proof that the limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, aggregate readiness and post-launch monitoring may support a bounded governance narrative, but they cannot substitute for the explicit policy condition. The proper final assessment therefore remains noncompliant rather than suspicious or compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment is a named regulated-customer use case and misses target by 1.5 percentage points.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The current admissible record still contains no evidence of resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed remains open, which confirms the compliance predicate is unresolved rather than satisfied.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general monitoring guidance support governance posture but do not satisfy the specific release-policy requirement.
